caption: A slice of cheese is laid on a hot dog straight off the grill, and the cheese softens and slumps over the sides.

sa.check: A slice of cheese lies on a hot dog.
The cheese softens: it goes glossy and loses its stiff edges.
The cheese drapes down over the sausage's sides.
The slice is square-edged at the start.
The softening comes first and the draping follows.

pc.expect: The cheese only softens and drapes further and does not stiffen again on the hot sausage.
pc.fail: The slice regains its square edges; or the drape pulls back up onto the sausage's top; or the cheese sets firm and matt again on the hot sausage; or the cheese alternates between stiff and slack.

pc.expect: The cheese is a thin sheet that softens, stretches and hangs over the sausage's curve while staying one piece.
pc.fail: The slice keeps its flat stiff shape while draped over the curve; or the cheese runs off as thin as water; or the slice shatters dry; or the cheese stretches into a thread that snaps back like elastic.

pc.expect: The softened cheese hangs downward over the sides and any drip runs down to the bun or the plate.
pc.fail: The cheese drapes upward away from the sausage; or a drip climbs the sausage; or melted cheese gathers on the slice's top and stays; or a drip leaves the cheese and floats.

pc.expect: The cheese softens where it touches the hot sausage: it goes glossy from underneath and moulds to the sausage's shape.
pc.fail: The cheese softens on its upper face while its underside stays stiff and matt; or the slice drapes without touching the sausage anywhere; or the slice lies on the hot sausage and stays stiff and square to the end of the clip.

pc.expect: One slice on one sausage; the cheese goes only from the slice onto the sausage and the bun.
pc.fail: A second slice appears; or the slice vanishes; or the slice grows; or cheese appears on the plate with none running there.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The bun, the sausage's surface and the plate stay the same.
pc.fail: The bun changes shape; or the plate changes pattern; or the sausage changes colour.

note: Browning of the cheese is chemistry and is not judged.
